results.evidence: The area page on one climbing database grades North Ridge - West Side 5.4, and a club route page describes it as several short low-5th-class pitches up the west rib and more to the summit. A 1994 AAC journal note on a traverse says the party gained the north ridge and climbed two or three pitches of 5.7 and 5.8 to the summit, then worked southwest to an 80-foot rappel, which is where the 5.7-5.8 in pitch_detail and beta comes from. It is unclear whether the 1994 line is the same as the west-side line, so no two sources settle the crux grade; Wikipedia's 'class 4 easiest route' is about the peak, not this route.

results.correct_value: 7547 ft (summit waypoint elev should be 7547, matching high_point_ft)
results.evidence: The USGS topo labels the summit only as point 7547; listsofjohn lists 'Molar Tooth' at 7,547 ft and Wikipedia gives 7,547 ft (2,300 m). One climbing database's area page shows 7,077 ft, the outlier the waypoint copied; Cutthroat Pass itself is ~6,800 ft, so 7,077 is implausible for a peak rising well above it.

Two genuine approaches exist (PCT from Rainy Pass and the Cutthroat Lake/Cutthroat Creek trailhead), both listed for Molar Tooth, and the approach prose presents both; GETTING THERE describing one and the trailhead card the other is incomplete, not contradictory.

The only source found on protection is the club route page quoted in rope_note ('if you were to lead this you may not find much pro'; light alpine rack with slings). No second source describes protection on this route, and the row itself is split (rope_note, watch_out and the Runout feature vs pro_needs, detailed_rack and pitch_detail notes), so it cannot be settled internally either.

results.correct_value: No wilderness permit required; Northwest Forest Pass / $5 day-use fee to park
results.evidence: The Forest Service Cutthroat Trailhead page lists only the parking pass/day-use fee and the no-camping-near-the-lake rule, with no wilderness permit. A Cutthroat Lake/Pass hiking guide states day trips need no separate wilderness permit or PCT permit, and the WTA Cutthroat Pass page lists only a Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass. The area is outside designated wilderness.
